name: Catalytic Interstitial Desiccation Drone CIDD-3 'Husk'
description:
The CIDD-3 is a slow-moving, high-endurance drone platform developed by HELIX BIOSYSTEMS as a derivative of their industrial tissue preservation research line. It operates by projecting a focused catalytic beam that accelerates osmotic pressure differentials across cell membranes in targeted tissue, rapidly drawing interstitial fluid outward through a process that mimics, at a greatly accelerated rate, the biochemical mechanisms of severe dehydration. Targets experience acute desiccation effects in exposed tissue — cracking skin, seizing muscles, intense thirst signals — without any actual systemic dehydration occurring, as the effect is surface-local and depth-limited to approximately 4cm of tissue penetration.

The drone's defining characteristic is its patience. The CIDD-3 is not designed for fast engagements. It moves slowly, hovers at a fixed standoff distance, and applies its catalytic beam in sustained, low-intensity pulses optimized for maximum discomfort over time rather than rapid incapacitation. Its autonomous target-lock system uses a proprietary HELIX BIOSYSTEMS moisture-differential sensor array to distinguish living targets from environmental objects with remarkable accuracy, and it will maintain lock on a moving target at walking pace indefinitely until its power cell is exhausted or it is physically destroyed.

Operators have noted that the CIDD-3 produces a faint, distinctive smell — a dry, slightly saline odor — that experienced field personnel have learned to recognize as an early warning. In enclosed environments, this olfactory signature is often the only indication of deployment before effects begin.
specifications: dimensions: 28cm x 14cm x 14cm operational speed: Max 4m/s (pursuit mode), 0.5m/s (sustained application mode) tissue penetration depth: Approximately 4cm effective range: 2m–10m targeting system: HELIX proprietary moisture-differential array power source: Long-duration lithium-polymer cell battery life: Up to 4 hours continuous operation weight: 1.8kg olfactory signature: Faint saline/dry atmosphere odor at close range
tactical_use: The CIDD-3 excels in siege and containment scenarios where operators want to make a position untenable over time without committing to direct engagement. A single drone deployed into a room or corridor will, within ten to fifteen minutes, make that space miserable enough that most unprotected occupants will seek to leave. Security teams use them to drive targets toward choke points. Interrogators use them in sustained sessions as an alternative to more legally complex methods. Some operators use multiple units in relay — one active, one charging — to maintain indefinite area presence.
cultural_context: Within GLMZ's corporate detention system, the CIDD-3 occupies a strange legal grey zone — it is licensed for use in 'compliance facilitation' contexts, a euphemism that has been dissected at length by civil rights advocates. Because it leaves no lasting injury in standard operating parameters, it rarely triggers the medical documentation requirements associated with more overtly damaging weapons. Street communities near processing centers refer to people who've been held in CIDD-3 environments as 'Husks' — a term that has spread beyond its origin to describe anyone visibly worn down by institutional pressure.
known_users: Freelance operators with corporate security licensing
story_hooks: Someone is deploying CIDD-3 units in the ventilation network of a residential block — residents are getting sick, the building management claims ignorance, and the drones keep disappearing before investigators arrive.
A HELIX BIOSYSTEMS licensing auditor has gone missing after flagging an anomalous pattern in CIDD-3 deployment logs across three different detention facilities run by the same shell company.

The players are trapped in a building with a malfunctioning CIDD-3 that has locked onto a target designation it cannot find — and its sensor array is broad enough that everyone in the building qualifies.

physical_description.visual_profile: A compact, deliberately unsexy hovering cube with a predatory patience built into its lines. The CIDD-3 resembles a small autonomous cube-drone, but its proportions are subtly off—slightly flattened, with weight distributed toward the center, making it look heavier and more grounded than typical aerial platforms. The front face features a dark, recessed lens array that doesn't reflect light the way cameras normally do; it absorbs it. This absence of reflection is deeply unsettling. The overall impression is clinical, almost medical—something that belongs in a sterile facility, not a combat zone.
physical_description.dimensions: 28cm L × 14cm W × 14cm H. Compact enough to fit in a large hand, awkward enough that no one wants to hold it for long.
physical_description.weight_description: Deceptively dense in hand—1.8kg distributed to feel heavier. The battery pack is mounted low, giving it a bottom-heavy quality that makes it feel anchored, purposeful. Not a weapon that feels nimble; it feels methodical.
physical_description.primary_material: Anodized aerospace-grade aluminum chassis with reinforced polymeric dampening mounts. The frame is rigid, designed to absorb vibration from sustained beam emission without drift.
physical_description.finish: Matte gunmetal gray with micro-texturing that kills reflections. The central lens array is deep matte black. Minimal shine anywhere—every surface treated to disappear into shadow.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray primary with black accent array and subtle teal indicator lines running along the power coupling points. Minimal branding.
physical_description.grip_texture: Not designed for gripping, but the corners are beveled with a slight rubberized grip compound for securing to mounting brackets.
distinctive_features: Central recessed lens array (moisture-differential sensor cluster) that sits dark and unreflective
Four discrete positioning vents (one per face) for thermal management
Faint teal LED indicators along power coupling edges—visible only when powered
Mounting hardpoint on undercarriage for deployment rig attachment
Micro-hairline seams where the catalytic emission chamber joins the main chassis
Heat-treated discoloration around the lens array (faint purple-gray hue from sustained beam testing)
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: HELIX BIOSYSTEMS logo (a double-helix motif) stamped in raised relief on the upper left face, approximately 2cm across. Below it: 'CIDD-3' model designation and a serial plate with batch code and manufacturing date. All markings are matte and small—designed for documentation, not advertising.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-used units show light scuffing on the mounting hardpoints and thermal discoloration (faint purple-gray oxidation) around the lens assembly from sustained operation. Battery housing develops minor stress marks from repeated charge cycles. Overall condition is meticulous—HELIX maintains these like laboratory equipment because that's what they are.
